jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Malawi has no AI-specific law, strategy or guidance yet. The only binding framework touching AI is the Data Protection Act, 2024, which gives people a right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing and is enforced by the communications regulator MACRA. A National AI Strategy is in draft consultation and an AI bill is planned.
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026, but Parliament's and the e-government department's websites could not be accessed and there is no official online gazette. The enacted text of the Data Protection Act, 2024 was not found online, so it is recorded from the bill as tabled. The draft AI strategy, the planned AI bill and an AI readiness report are tracked as leads. Malawi is marked for a later retry and, as a country of over 20 million people with few records, for a longer catch-up pass.

instruments.current_status: The enacted Act's text and its Gazette publication were not found online on any official site. The text read is the Bill as tabled in Parliament (Data Protection Bill, 2023, B. No. 22), hosted by the Public Private Partnership Commission's Digital Malawi Project; clause 25 of the Bill gives the right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing. In-force status rests on MACRA's August 2026 public notice on unlawful processing of personal data (https://macra.mw/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/PUBLIC-NOTICE-Unlawful-Processing-of-Personal-Data-1.pdf), in which MACRA, as designated Data Protection Authority, enforces the Data Protection Act, 2024 and cites its section 49. Act number, commencement date and final section numbering are unverified.
instruments.summary: Malawi's comprehensive data protection law, designating the Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority (MACRA) as Data Protection Authority and setting principles for lawful, fair and transparent processing of personal data of natural persons. In the Bill text it gives data subjects the right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produce legal or similarly significant effects, and requires controllers to disclose the existence of automated decision-making. It also imposes security and breach-notification duties, regulates cross-border transfers and requires registration of data controllers and processors of significant importance.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only binding Malawian law found that governs AI use: automated decision-making and profiling rights, enforced by MACRA.
